name: global-arrays
desc: Partitioned Global Address Space (PGAS) library for distributed arrays
why: A PGAS distributed array library is an interesting model of global memory, but it is mostly plumbing for HPC.

brief.what_it_is: Global Arrays (GA) is a library for distributed dense arrays that presents them as one global array. Application code, written against its C, Fortran, or GA++ C++ interface, reads and writes array sections with one-sided Get, Put, and Accumulate calls and does atomic read-increment operations, without needing to know which node holds the data. The library bundles the ComEx communication runtime, the MA memory allocator, parallel I/O libraries (DRA, EAF, SF), and TCGMSG/TCGMSG-MPI. The homepage says it supports both blocking and non-blocking primitives.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes GA as a Partitioned Global Address Space programming model that gives shared-memory-like access to distributed arrays. The README frames it as augmenting the message-passing model with that shared-memory-style access.
brief.how_it_works: GA uses ComEx, its communication runtime, to abstract inter-node communication, and ComEx replaced ARMCI starting with GA v5.4. The default ComEx ports use MPI, and most ComEx implementations use on-node shared memory for faster communication within a node. The homepage says GA supports location consistency.
brief.install_notes: Neither the homepage nor the GitHub README I read includes build or install steps, required dependencies, or configuration. The README links to a full manual on readthedocs, which I did not fetch, so build details (MPI, compilers, configure options) remain unverified. The homepage links to release notes and a download page, but I did not see a version number.
brief.standout: Its PGAS model is built on one-sided operations over dense arrays, with an MPI-based communication layer that also uses shared memory inside a node. It has been around long enough to carry its own ARMCI-to-ComEx transition and a bundled set of parallel I/O libraries.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage has a Latest Release section but shows no version or date. The GitHub README has a CI badge, a link to a GitHub issue tracker, and says the most recent development funding came from the Exascale Computing Project. I found no release date or last-commit date, so I cannot confirm whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The README calls TCGMSG obsolete and ARMCI deprecated, so parts of the bundle are legacy. It is aimed at high-performance computing and dense arrays; DRA works only on two-dimensional arrays. The license is BSD 3-Clause, per the README badge. The scout note says it is mostly plumbing for HPC, and the sources I read support that. Build details were not visible in what I fetched.
quotes: Global Arrays (GA) is a Partitioned Global Address Space (PGAS) programming model.
The default ComEx ports use MPI --- which makes GA and ComEx portable for high-end systems.
It augments the message-passing model by providing a shared-memory like access to distributed dense arrays.
